meta.what: engineered low-speed hind-leg cycle for one lizard2 leg -- the fitting target an A/B structural comparison is run against
meta.status: engineered. No field here is a Komodo measurement, and this file is not a design decision; it exists so two candidate chains can be scored on the same target.

labels.gait.period_s: engineered (chosen so the cycle is slow enough for a walking gait)
labels.gait.speed_m_per_s: paper_reported as a cross-species reference (M08 walk, V. exanthematicus 0.29 m/s, range 0.24-0.34) -- NOT a Komodo value
labels.gait.hind_duty: paper_reported (M08 same source: hindlimb stance 69 +/- 1.7 % of cycle)
labels.phases[].dx_m / dz_m: engineered, derived in gait.derivation from the three values above
labels.phases[].thigh_elev_deg: the femur's elevation off the HORIZONTAL PLANE (negative = pointing down), per this file's own definition: elevation = atan2(femur_z, hypot(femur_x, femur_y)), so the lateral component is NOT dropped -- an x-z projection once read a sprawling femur as a vertical one. The single anchor (0.0 = level, at mid-stance) is a crude guess from a camera frame and is PENDING a measurement: the rig's own solution at that phase sits near -34.6 deg with the femur almost entirely lateral, so do not read the anchor as an animal value and do not read the gap as a conflict until both sides are stated in this same definition
labels.body.base_z_m: engineering choice, equal to the checker's own default so a reading is comparable with the existing pose prints

missing: thigh and shank direction over the cycle (one mid-stance anchor only)
pad yaw and lateral foot position over the cycle (y is left at the asset's own zero pose)
torso, spine and tail motion; body height variation over the cycle
forelimbs and the other three legs (the mirror rule for those is in the r1 record, section 11)
passive joint range: no varanid ROM values exist to bound this target (see 2026-09-29-varanid-joint-range-of-motion-evidence.md)
meta.derivation: stance_sweep = speed * duty * period = 0.3 * 0.69 * 1.2 = 0.2484 m. The foot travels that far aft over the body while planted, so dx runs +sweep/2 -> -sweep/2 across stance and back across swing; the body itself advances speed * period = 0.36 m per cycle.

stance_reference_note: a stance phase's dz is measured against the pad ORIGIN's standing height, but a contact is made by the pad's SOLE; the tool lifts the standing sole onto the floor (its own lowest vertex, read from the asset) before applying dz, otherwise the cycle asks for a contact the pad cannot have. Measured 2026-10-08: at body height 0.9 m the standing sole already sits ~6 mm under the floor, so without this the stance read ~5-6 mm of penetration that looked like a chain failure and was a target-definition error

posture.status: CANDIDATE bands, not measurements and not approved. The rejection the user asked for is the low end of the azimuth band: a femur inside the sagittal plane (azimuth -> 0) is the upright, adducted 'dog' gait, and a similar footfall timing can carry either posture, which is why this criterion is spatial rather than temporal. The bands' motivation is that varanids sprawl and add femoral adduction and long-axis rotation to lengthen the stride (Clemente 2011/2013, cited in 2026-09-29-varanid-joint-range-of-motion-evidence.md); the numbers themselves are this file's own engineering choice and the pitch axis is missing from the asset entirely
posture.measured_from: the femur vector, elevation = atan2(z, hypot(x, y)) and azimuth = atan2(y, x), both in base_link, so the lateral component is never dropped

body.note: level body, no yaw; a turning or rolling body is out of scope for v0

facing.note: checked and flagged, never fitted: the objective is position plus a priced joint excursion, so no criterion below can be paid off with a smaller position error

tolerances.note: exploration thresholds, not approved values: none of these has been shown sufficient. joint_step_rad 0.35 is 20.1 deg, over the target's own sampling interval of 0.1 s; the joint rate is also read against the URDF's OWN velocity limit, which is a physical bound rather than a chosen one
